mechanism_class: damage-scaling: payload as a percentage of the TARGET's (corpse's) maximum life
spec_text_or_path: Detonate Dead's defining identity: the explosion deals 6-7.9% of the DETONATED CORPSE'S maximum life as fire AoE — damage scales off the VICTIM'S body, not the caster's stats. Boss-tier corpses produce massive explosions; higher-life map monsters (red maps) yield bigger blasts, so the build gets stronger as monster HP pools grow. The engine damage model scales off CASTER stats + base_mag exclusively; there is NO lane for 'damage = fraction of the target's/corpse's maximum HP'. The corpse-as-AMMUNITION economy IS covered natively (charge_stack_sub_shape=accumulator, accumulator_fill_trigger=on-corpse-consume, resource_economy.py:142) — Desecrate refills the pool — but that is the fuel-supply, not the damage-scaling. Ladder audit: map (fire ground_targeted_circle OK) -> approximate+note (mapped as standard caster-scaled fire-AoE; the victim-HP-scaling is LOST, a player would notice their blast no longer grows with corpse/monster health) -> quantitative mint N/A (this is not a range/count extension of an existing parameter; there is no target-HP-scaling parameter to widen) -> qualitative mint-candidate: a 'target-max-HP-fraction damage source' primitive (a new damage-scaling mechanism, evidence-gated). Volatile Dead (autonomous corpse-seeking sibling) and D2/D3/D4 corpse-explosion and Cremation would share this substrate — steward should check accrual across the corpus before minting. Destination: either (a) a target-HP-fraction damage primitive, or (b) an explicit ruling that corpse/monster-HP-scaling is flavor-only and the caster-scaled-fire-AoE approximation is canonical for the whole corpse-explosion family.

mechanism_class: per-attack RANDOM element selection from a fixed pool, with pool-pruning to force a single element
spec_text_or_path: Elemental Hit's defining identity: EACH attack rolls ONE random element from {fire, cold, lightning} at large values (never mixing on a single hit), and the build-defining Combat Focus threshold jewels DELETE unwanted elements from the pool (Crimson blocks cold, Viridian blocks lightning) to FORCE consistent single-element rolls. The signature item (Combat Focus) exists PRECISELY to sculpt this random pool. The engine fixes ONE element per skill at generation time — there is no per-attack-random-element-roll, and no element-pool-pruning mechanic. Ladder audit: map (multi_projectile bow-shot OK) -> approximate+note (mapped to the meta ENDPOINT: forced mono-fire via ELEMENT_CONVERSION_MONO; captures where the build LANDS but LOSES the random-roll-then-curate-the-pool mechanic that IS the gameplay and the reason the signature jewels exist; graded APPROX) -> quantitative mint N/A (not a range/count widen of an existing param) -> qualitative mint-candidate: a 'per-hit random-element-from-pool + pool-membership-pruning' primitive (new mechanism, evidence-gated). Related PoE kits sharing an RNG-element or roll-from-pool substrate (e.g. Wild Strike, Molten Strike element-partition, Spectrum-gem variants) may accrue — steward should check before minting; if only Elemental Hit forces it, the mono-conversion approximation may be ruled canonical. Destination: either (a) an RNG-element-pool + pruning primitive, or (b) an explicit ruling that per-attack element randomization is out of scope and mono-conversion-endpoint is the canonical map for roll-from-pool bow skills.
